correctness.rationale: Every pair of distinct four-cycles shares 0, 1, or 2 edges: 0/1 gives joint probability 1/64, a two-edge path gives 1/32, and opposite shared edges give 0. These last unions are uniquely K2,3 and K4 edge-subgraphs, with three cycle pairs each. Thus the variance identity follows exactly. For the cube, three incident squares require pairwise opposite directions among three incident edges, impossible. All 486 four- and five-vertex labelled graphs containing four-cycles, K6, and all 4096 cube orientations passed an independently specified integer-count checker; the general proof is combinatorial, not inferred from this finite cutoff.

value.rationale: The complete motif classification answers a structural question over every fixed graph, distinguishing positive and negative dependence, giving the iff forbidden-subgraph criterion and making second moments detect exact higher-order motif imbalance. The cube shows a nontrivial three-wise obstruction despite independence of every pair. These are mathematically natural graph-probability properties, not arbitrary parameter slices or known-table recomputation.
